title: Week 2 Test — Multiplication Masters A
note: Drawn from Juniper's week-2 math lessons (times table review 2-5, equal groups & arrays, word problems with arrays, estimate to check) plus the daily spine practice activities.

questions.why: Zero groups of anything is nothing — you've got this!
Four groups means four 2s added together — you spotted the pattern!

questions.q: An array has 3 rows and 4 columns. How many dots in all?
questions.why: Rows × columns: 3 × 4 = 12 — your array eyes are sharp!

questions.q: There are 4 bags. Each bag has 5 apples. How many apples in total?
questions.why: 4 groups of 5: draw 4 circles with 5 dots each, count them up — 20!

questions.q: A garden has 3 rows of flowers. Each row has 6 flowers. Which multiplication sentence matches?
questions.why: Rows × flowers in each row — you're reading the story like a math detective!
4 × 6 is exactly 24 — your estimate was right on target!

questions.q: Which fact would you check by estimating 5 × 5 ≈ 25?
questions.why: Estimating 5 × 5 as 25 helps you know the answer makes sense — smart checking!

questions.q: Draw an array for 2 × 5. How many dots?
questions.why: 2 rows of 5 dots each — count by 5s: 5, 10. You've got array power!
Counting by 2s — each step adds 2 more. You're cruising through the tables!
